rationale: Evaluating omission of required braking requires characterising whether braking is needed and whether the vehicle performs it. SG-1 and FR-7 establish braking behaviour itself as the subject of evaluation, while H-1 establishes the relevance of stopping in time to avoid collision. P remains focused on that behaviour and its operational context rather than incorporating sensing, computation, communication, or controller mechanisms.
determining_elements: The vehicle’s 'braking-behaviour state' directly addresses performance or omission of the braking maneuvers required by SG-1 and FR-7.
Situations requiring braking to avoid collision with obstacles or road users are supported by H-1 and FR-7; the scope is not restricted to the single illustrative pedestrian scenario.
Whether braking occurs in time concerns the braking behaviour itself, supported by H-1’s failure-to-stop-in-time event and FR-7.1’s braking-onset requirement.
The scope references obstacle-detection situations as operational context without making detection processes, sensor failures, or controller internals part of P.
